issue.title: No audio alerts on Skydroid G20 (Android 13) with QGC 5.1.x, works correctly with QGC 5.0.8
issue.body:
### Have you checked the latest release for fixes?

- [x] Yes, I’ve tested on the latest release

### Description

**Expected Behavior**

Audio alerts should function normally on the Skydroid G20.

Pressing the "Test" button in Application Settings > General > Audio Output Volume should play the test sound.

MAVLink voice notifications and warning messages should also be audible during operation.

**Current Behavior**

No audio is produced when pressing the "Test" button.

MAVLink voice notifications and warning messages are also completely silent.

Android audio itself is working correctly:
- YouTube audio works normally.
- Android Text-To-Speech works normally.
- Device speaker functions correctly.
- QGroundControl audio volume is set to 100%.

The issue only occurs with recent QGroundControl builds.

Audio works correctly with QGroundControl 5.0.6 and 5.0.8 on the same hardware.

**Steps To Reproduce**

1. Install the latest QGroundControl Android Daily Build on a Skydroid G20 running Android 13.
2. Launch QGroundControl.
3. Open Application Settings > General.
4. Set Audio Output Volume to 100%.
5. Press the "Test" button.
6. No sound is produced.
7. Connect to a vehicle and trigger MAVLink status messages or warnings.
8. No voice notifications are heard.

**Additional Details**

System Information

QGC Version: Daily v5.0.3-1056-gbd80a5cff (64 bit)
QGC Build: Daily
Operating System: Android 13
Flight Controller: CubePilot Cube Orange+
Autopilot Software (with version): ArduCopter 4.6.3

Hardware:
- Skydroid G20
- Android 13

Comparison testing:

- QGroundControl 5.0.6 (64-bit Stable): Audio works correctly
- QGroundControl 5.0.8 (64-bit Stable): Audio works correctly
- QGroundControl Daily v5.0.3-1056-gbd80a5cff (64-bit): No audio output

The issue is fully reproducible on the same device by switching between versions.

The problem affects both:
- The built-in audio test function
- MAVLink voice notifications and warnings

Because the audio test button itself is silent, the issue appears to be unrelated to MAVLink communication and may be related to audio output handling introduced in recent builds.

I can reliably reproduce the issue by installing QGroundControl 5.0.8 and the latest Daily Build on the same Skydroid G20 device. Audio works immediately on 5.0.8 and fails immediately on the Daily Build with no other changes to the hardware or Android configuration.

### Platform

Android

### Flight Stack

ArduPilot

### System Information

QGC Version: Daily v5.0.3-1056-gbd80a5cff (64 bit)

QGC Build: Daily

Operating System: Android 13 (Skydroid G20)

Flight Controller: CubePilot Cube Orange+

Autopilot Software (with version): ArduCopter 4.6.3

### Log Files and Screenshots

_No response_

14504.title: fix(Android): declare TTS_SERVICE query so QTextToSpeech finds the system engine
14504.body:
## Problem

Voice announcements don't work on Android 12/13 (QGC daily). `AudioOutput::init()` logs *"No available QTextToSpeech engines found"* and bails, so every `say()` is a no-op.

## Root cause

QGC targets **minSdk 31 / target SDK 35**. Since Android 11 (API 30), [package visibility filtering](https://developer.android.com/training/package-visibility) hides other apps/services unless the manifest declares a `<queries>` element. The system TTS engine is a separate service, and `android/AndroidManifest.xml` declared queries for USB/Bluetooth intents but **not** for TTS. As a result:

- `QTextToSpeech::availableEngines()` returns empty
- `AudioOutput::init()` returns early (`src/Utilities/Audio/AudioOutput.cc:65-68`)
- `_initialized` stays false, so `say()` no-ops

## Fix

Add the documented Qt-on-Android `<queries>` declaration for the TTS service:

```xml
<queries>
    <intent>
        <action android:name="android.intent.action.TTS_SERVICE" />
    </intent>
</queries>
```

## Testing

Rebuild the APK; with `Utilities.AudioOutput` debug logging enabled the log now shows `TTS Engine set to: android` instead of the "No available engines" warning. Voice announcements and the in-app audio test work on a device with a TTS engine installed (Google TTS by default).

Fixes mavlink/qgroundcontrol#14469
Fixes #14521

## Pull request overview

Fixes Android 11+ package visibility constraints so QGroundControl’s `QTextToSpeech` can discover the system TTS engine, restoring voice announcements on newer Android versions.

**Changes:**
- Adds an Android manifest `<queries>` entry for the `android.intent.action.TTS_SERVICE` intent so the system TTS service is visible to the app.

pr:14504.message:
fix(Android): bundle the TextToSpeech backend plugin so speech works

QTextToSpeech::availableEngines() returned empty on Android, so
AudioOutput::init() bailed and voice announcements never started.

Root cause: Qt6::TextToSpeech was linked PRIVATE into the static QGCAudio
library. A PRIVATE module link into a STATIC lib propagates the library for
linking (via $<LINK_ONLY:>) but strips its INTERFACE_QT_PLUGIN_TARGETS
compile property, so androiddeployqt never added the Android TTS backend
plugin (libplugins_texttospeech_qttexttospeech_android) to
android-deploy-plugins. The module .so shipped but no backend plugin did,
leaving availableEngines() empty. Link it PUBLIC so the plugin-target
property reaches the app target, exactly as the position/sensors/multimedia
plugins are deployed.

Also declare the TTS_SERVICE <queries> entry for Android 11+ package
visibility. Not strictly required on every device (the framework binds the
default public engine via the system service), but it is the documented
requirement and guards stricter ROMs where the app-side getEngines() path
is filtered.

While here, harden AudioOutput against the QTextToSpeech API contract:
- Run the queue check, enqueue(), and counter update in one slot dispatched
  to the engine thread. qReturnArg can't capture a return value across a
  queued invokeMethod, and all queue/counter mutation must stay on the
  engine thread; this removes the cross-thread race and lets _textQueueSize
  be a plain qsizetype.
- Zero _textQueueSize on stateChanged(Ready) (the queue is provably drained
  there) instead of decrementing on aboutToSynthesize, which fires when an
  utterance starts, not when it finishes.
- Always connect errorOccurred (not just in debug builds) and reset the
  queue depth on error so a recovered engine isn't wedged in the
  over-limit branch; log enqueue() failures with state()/errorReason().
- Construct QTextToSpeech with the default (auto-selected) engine instead of
  building the "none" backend then setEngine(""); apply locale, an explicit
  voice, and the cached Speak capability via _applyEngineSettings().
- Use BoundaryHint::Immediate for the mute / queue-overflow / test stop().
- Fix _replaceAbbreviations: tokenize -> map each token -> rejoin, instead
  of N whole-string replace() calls that over-matched substrings across
  tokens and mismatched case.
- Defer initialization until the engine reaches Ready instead of bailing on
  a not-yet-ready engine. The Android backend initializes asynchronously, so
  a synchronous state()/engine() check at startup could return early with no
  retry; init() now wires stateChanged first and finalizes in _finishInit()
  on the Ready transition. Guard _applyEngineSettings() on Ready so locale /
  voice enumeration never runs against an empty engine.

Fixes #14469
